chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the mature woman (thayyib) who proposes marriage to herself. He said, 'Yes, she has more authority over herself; she may appoint herself to whomever she wishes, provided he is her equal (kufu'), after she has previously been married to a husband.'

key_terms.أَمْلَكُ بِنَفْسِهَا: She has more authority/ownership over herself
key_terms.الثَّيِّب: A mature woman who has previously been married

ai.seo_question: Does a mature woman need a male guardian to contract her own marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between a virgin (bikr) and a mature, previously married woman (thayyib) in Shia jurisprudence, granting the latter full autonomy to contract her own marriage without a wali's consent. The condition of 'kufu'' (compatibility/equality) ensures that her choice aligns with social and familial standards, reflecting the juristic principle that prior marriage experience confers greater legal independence. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the woman's agency in marital affairs, contrasting with schools that require a guardian for all women regardless of marital history.
